sources.entry: KeyCastr - KeyCastr, an open-source keystroke visualizer. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/keycastr/keycastr) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: KeyCastr is an open-source macOS keystroke visualizer that shows your keystrokes and optionally mouse clicks on screen for screencasts, presentations, and collaboration.
summary.what_it_does: KeyCastr displays keystrokes on screen so viewers can follow what is being typed during screencasts, presentations, or collaborative sessions. Users can choose to show command keys, all modified keys, or all keystrokes. It can also include mouse clicks. The displayed keystroke overlay can be repositioned by clicking and dragging the text, and it defaults to the bottom left of the display. The README says it has a Default and a Svelte visualizer, and that developers can build their own visualizers on top of KeyCastr. Setup requires granting macOS Input Monitoring or Accessibility permission so the app can receive input events. Updates are handled through the Sparkle framework, which the README says is the only networking mechanism.
use_cases: Showing keystrokes in screencasts or tutorial videos
Demonstrating keyboard commands to remote collaborators
Building a custom keystroke visualizer on top of KeyCastr
how_to_run: Download the latest release from the GitHub releases page
Launch KeyCastr and grant permission under Security & Privacy > Input Monitoring (macOS 10.15+) or Accessibility (older macOS)
Choose which keys to display (command keys, modified keys, or all keystrokes) and optionally enable mouse clicks
Drag the on-screen text to reposition it if needed
notable: Display modes: command keys, all modified keys, or all keystrokes, with optional mouse click display
Pluggable visualizers: a Default and a Svelte visualizer, with support for building custom ones
Free and open source under BSD 3-Clause, available since 2009
README states it does not send networking traffic except through Sparkle update checks, and does not display password entry in secure fields
caveats: macOS only; requires Input Monitoring or Accessibility permission, which grants broad input access
Troubleshooting may be needed if permissions are not granted or the window is offscreen
